## Federal Reserve Federal Funds Rate Target Range at End of Q1 2026

At the conclusion of the first quarter of 2026, the Federal Reserve maintained its federal funds rate target range at **3.50% to 3.75%**. This decision was formalized at the FOMC's March 18, 2026 meeting, where the Committee voted to hold rates steady [7].

The rate had remained unchanged since late 2025, following three consecutive rate cuts beginning in September 2025 [5]. The January 2026 FOMC meeting — the first of the year — also held the target range steady at 3.50%–3.75%, signaling a cautious and data-dependent pause in the easing cycle [5].

At the March meeting, the FOMC's decision to hold was not unanimous; one member dissented in favor of a 25-basis-point cut [6]. The Fed's updated economic projections reflected growing concern about inflation, with the core PCE forecast for 2026 revised upward to 2.7%, while the growth forecast was simultaneously raised to 2.4% [6]. Federal Reserve Chair Powell acknowledged that tariff-related uncertainty was complicating the inflation outlook and that the Committee preferred to wait for clearer data before adjusting policy further [5].

The official FOMC statement noted that while economic activity was expanding at a solid pace, inflation remained "somewhat elevated" relative to the Fed's 2% target, and job gains had slowed [7]. The Committee emphasized a careful, data-driven approach to any future adjustments.

Looking ahead, the median FOMC member projected one additional rate cut in 2026 and one more in 2027, ultimately bringing the federal funds rate to approximately 3.125% [6]. FRED data confirms the upper limit of the target range stood at **3.75%** as of March 31, 2026, consistent across subsequent weeks into late May 2026 [1].

In summary, the federal funds rate target range at the end of Q1 2026 was firmly set at **3.50%–3.75%**, reflecting the Fed's cautious stance amid persistent inflation and broader economic uncertainty.
